Judge whether the copy matches the brand voice.
Voice guidelines: ['Write plainly and specifically; name the feature and what it does.', "Lead with the customer's trip, not the product's ego.", 'Prefer concrete numbers (weight, capacity, ratings) over adjectives.', "Respect the reader's experience; assume they know the outdoors.", 'Be honest about limits — say what the gear is not built for.', 'One clear call to action per message.']
Tone descriptors: ['grounded', 'practical', 'warm', 'understated', 'trail-tested', 'unpretentious']
Terms to avoid: ['guaranteed', 'miracle', 'risk-free', 'best ever', 'cure', '100% safe', 'unbreakable', 'lifetime warranty', 'revolutionary', "world's best", 'bulletproof']
Subject: What's new at camp this season
Preview: A few things worth knowing before your next trip.
Body: Hey,

No big announcements this time — just a note to check in as the season moves along.

If you've been out recently, you know the conditions have been variable. Shoulder season has a way of humbling even well-planned trips. Layers you didn't think you'd need, water sources that weren't where the map said, campsites that looked better in photos.

We've been paying attention to what people are actually running into out there, and we're working on bringing in gear that speaks to those real situations — not the curated highlight-reel version of a trip, but the version where you're problem-solving at mile 14.

More specifics coming soon. In the meantime, if there's something you've been looking for and haven't found — a particular weight range, a feature set, a use case we haven't covered — reply to this email. We read them.

Thanks for being on the list. We'll keep it useful.

— The Team
Score 0-1; a score below 0.75 is a fail.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no prose or code fences. Reason first, then decide — the verdict must follow from the reasoning. Use exactly this key order: {"reasoning": "<one sentence>", "evidence": ["<short quote or fact>", ...], "score": <float 0-1>, "verdict": "pass"|"fail"}.
